ops.body:
Homebrew marks every **cask** download with `com.apple.quarantine`. A **formula** download does not. For a CLI this is the difference between a binary that runs on arrival and one whose first exec blocks on a syspolicyd assessment (see the note on `spctl` passing while exec hangs).

Observed across yasyf's tap on 2026-09-21: ccx and cc-notes released from the same shared `yasyf/homebrew-tap` `release-go.yml` and ran immediately; cc-patch, released from that same workflow minutes apart, hung — the only difference being that cc-patch declared `homebrew_casks:` in `.goreleaser.yaml` while the other two use `render-formula`.

A cask compounds it when it has a `postflight`. cc-patch's ran `cc-patch install-daemons` from the staged path, so the first exec of the quarantined binary happened *inside* `brew install`, turning a hung command into a hung install.

Notarization is orthogonal and is **not** given up by moving to a formula: goreleaser's `notarize:` block keys on the **build id**, not on the homebrew block, so archives stay signed and notarized either way. What a formula gives up is the cask's install hooks — anything a postflight did becomes a `caveats` line.

**Choosing between them.** Cask for a `.app` bundle or anything wanting install hooks. Formula for a plain CLI, which is also what the shared workflow's own header recommends. Switching costs three edits in the repo: delete `homebrew_casks:` from `.goreleaser.yaml`, add `.github/formula/<name>.rb.tmpl`, and set `render-formula: true` plus `formula-template`/`formula-name` in `release.yml`.

**One sharp edge.** The pinned `render-formula` action's automatic sha lookup demands all four archives — `darwin_{arm64,amd64}` and `linux_{arm64,amd64}` — and hard-errors on any that is missing, with no input to skip it. A darwin-only tool such as cc-patch therefore cannot use the formula path until that action tolerates an absent arch. Both existing formula callers (ccx, synckitd) ship all four, which is why the limit had not been hit.
**Outcome for cc-patch, 2026-09-21: it stayed a cask.** The four-arch limit above is the reason, and it is recorded so nobody re-derives it. Moving cc-patch to a formula would have required changing `render-formula` in `yasyf/homebrew-tap`, a workflow twenty-one packages share, to tolerate a darwin-only tool — not worth it for one binary.

The cask fix instead, in cc-patch's own `.goreleaser.yaml`: the postflight strips `com.apple.quarantine` from the staged binary, **before** the `install-daemons` call. That ordering is the whole fix, not the presence of the strip — `install-daemons` is the binary's first exec, so a postflight clearing quarantine afterwards still hangs, and hangs inside `brew install`. `must_succeed: false`, because `xattr -d` exits 1 with `No such xattr` when the attribute is absent, which is every re-run on a clean staged path.

The launchd copy at `~/.daemonkit/bin/cc-patch` needs no strip: `placeProgram` reads bytes and writes a new file, and an xattr belongs to the file rather than its contents. Verified against a deliberately quarantined source, with `cp -p` as the positive control that does carry it.

So a cask shipping a plain CLI is fine **provided its postflight strips quarantine before anything execs the payload**. The formula's advantage is that it never needs that step at all.
